audit_focus: Inlined values that should be env-sourced (and vice versa)
PII / real email leakage in fixtures
Auth bypass via cookies / sessionStorage / addInitScript
page.route(...) mocking that would hide backend security checks

hardcoded_secrets.details: Only credential-like string is `password = 'Test1234!'` (line 20). Generic synthetic test password paired with `@test.local` reserved-style domain — not a real secret. No API keys, tokens, connection strings, private keys, or bearer tokens present. gitleaks default rule set does not match this pattern (no high-entropy/base64/AKIA/sk-/etc. shapes).

env_handling.details: Spec references no `process.env` / `import.meta.env` / `playwright`-level env vars. All values are derived in-process via `Date.now()`, so the test is self-contained and will not silently pass/fail based on missing CI secrets. Base URL is implicit (relative URLs `/auth/register`, `/dashboard`, …) and resolved by `playwright.config.ts`, which is the correct boundary for that value.

pii_in_fixtures.details: Email pattern `e2e-projects-${Date.now()}@test.local` uses the `.local` mDNS-reserved suffix (RFC 6762), which cannot be a real, deliverable address. Project names (`Acme`, `Brand X`) are non-personal trademarks/placeholders. No real names, phones, or addresses present.

auth_bypass.details: No `context.addCookies`, `page.context().addInitScript`, `sessionStorage`/`localStorage` writes, `setExtraHTTPHeaders`, or storage-state injection. Authentication is exercised end-to-end through the real `/auth/register` form (lines 27–32), which means the test traverses the production code path including any CSRF/session/auth guards. Any future regression in those guards will surface in this spec rather than be masked.

backend_mocking.details: No `page.route(...)` / `page.unroute(...)` / `fulfill(...)` / `abort(...)` calls anywhere in the file. All requests hit the real backend, so server-side validation (e.g. name length, RBAC on project ownership, soft-delete authorization) is genuinely exercised.

owasp_relevance.details: OWASP Top 10 categories apply to the system under test, not to a Playwright spec. This spec is a black-box test consumer and does not itself author auth, crypto, queries, deserialization, or SSRF surfaces. It exercises (but does not weaken) those controls in the real backend.

verdict_reasoning: The spec contains no hardcoded secrets, no real PII, no environment-variable leaks, no auth bypass, and no route mocking that would mask backend security checks. The single password literal `Test1234!` is a non-secret synthetic test value paired with a `.local` reserved domain — the explicit pattern AC-T8 permits. The test exercises the real auth and CRUD endpoints end-to-end, which is exactly what a golden-path E2E should do from a security perspective. Approved.
